summary: Defines requirements for a set of tools to be used by the IETF Nominations Committee, which selects people for leadership positions. It lists what the tools should do to support the committee's work. It is informational.

eli5.summary: A group that picks team leaders needs good checklists and forms. This memo lists what those tools must do so the picking goes smoothly.

questions: what tools does the nominations committee need
subtitle: Tools to help the committee that picks IETF leaders work smoothly and securely.

tldr.problem: The IETF Nominations Committee needs to securely collect nominations, feedback, and questionnaires from the community to select leaders, but this process requires managing sensitive information with strong encryption and access controls.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC specifies requirements for web-based tools that authenticate users at three levels (community member, NomCom member, and NomCom chair), encrypt all sensitive communications, manage nominations and responses, and organize community feedback about candidates.
tldr.outcome: Organizations implementing NomCom tools can follow these requirements to build systems that protect confidentiality while enabling efficient leadership selection.

today: RFC 6730 is an Informational document describing requirements that were designed to improve the existing NomCom tools. The IETF has implemented tools following or inspired by these requirements to support the annual leadership selection process.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The IETF Nominations Committee (NomCom) is the body responsible for selecting candidates to fill open positions in the Internet Engineering Steering Group (IESG), the Internet Architecture Board (IAB), and the Internet Administrative Oversight Committee (IAOC). This process requires collecting nominations from the community, accepting or declining from nominees, gathering questionnaires, and most importantly, collecting confidential feedback about candidates. To do this work efficiently and securely, the NomCom needs specialized tools.

This RFC describes the requirements that these tools must meet. It covers everything from user authentication and data encryption to how nominations should be tracked and how community feedback should be collected and organized.
sections.eli5: A group picks leaders for the Internet. They need secret forms to collect votes and feedback safely, so nobody knows who said what about whom.

sections.title: Authentication and Access Control
sections.content:
The NomCom tool must support three distinct levels of user access. Community members access a public interface to submit nominations and feedback. NomCom members access a private interface where they can enter nominations on behalf of community members, provide feedback, and review candidate materials. The NomCom chair has full administrative access to configure forms, send emails, and manage the overall process.

All users authenticate using the IETF's datatracker system, which centralizes credential management. The Secretariat staff set up access control lists to assign roles, but importantly, Secretariat staff themselves have no access to the sensitive data the tool stores.
sections.eli5: Three groups use the tool: regular members (read-only), committee members (add stuff), and the chair (boss). Everyone logs in the same way, but the tool remembers what each person is allowed to do.

sections.title: Managing Nominations
sections.content:
The tool must allow community members to nominate people for open positions and automatically sends each nominee an email telling them they were nominated, without revealing who nominated them. Nominees can then accept or decline using links in that email. The NomCom chair can also manually enter nominees from nominations the committee receives offline, and can mark people who received multiple nominations for the same position as the same candidate.

The tool tracks which nominees have accepted and which have declined, provides reports by position and by nominee, and can send automatic reminders to people who haven't yet responded. The chair can customize all the messages the tool sends.
sections.eli5: The tool collects names of people to consider, tells them they're being considered (secretly), and tracks who said yes or no.

sections.title: Questionnaires and Feedback
sections.content:
Each open position has its own questionnaire that the NomCom chair creates. Nominees who accept their nomination fill out the questionnaire for each position and email it to the NomCom mailing list. The tool tracks which nominees have submitted questionnaires for which positions.

Community feedback is crucial: anyone can submit feedback about any accepting nominee to the public interface. NomCom members can submit feedback to the private interface, optionally anonymously. All questionnaires and feedback submitted via email to the NomCom list are automatically archived, and the chair can route any archive email into a nominee's feedback section if that email discusses multiple candidates or positions.
sections.eli5: Each candidate fills out a form. Anyone can write down what they think about a candidate. The tool stores all these opinions so the committee can read them.

sections.title: Security and Data Protection
sections.content:
All communications involving the NomCom, including feedback, questionnaires, and internal discussions, must be encrypted before being stored. The NomCom chair generates a public/private key pair (typically using OpenSSL) and enters the public key into the tool. All sensitive data is then encrypted with this public key before being saved to persistent storage. When NomCom members log in, they enter their private key, which the tool uses to decrypt data but never saves. After the NomCom's term ends, the chair can delete all data collected by the committee, but the tool protects data from the next year's NomCom.

Importantly, the system is designed so that even system administrators cannot see sensitive data at rest. The encryption key is only available to NomCom members during their active session.
sections.eli5: All the secret stuff gets locked in a chest with a puzzle lock. Committee members have the puzzle key, but they have to bring it with them each time. When they leave, the key goes away.
